exceptions.reason: The kit is the one ui folder: wrappers live here (Q59) and core's components/ui re-exports them. Add-ons and core import no Base UI, which is stricter than the skill (ui-conventions.md, rules 1 and 4).
The kit's token file, shared on purpose with marketplace kit apps; apps/core/src/index.css imports it and is the desktop's one stylesheet.
Syntax colouring for the Markdown preview, loaded with Notepad's lazy chunk only so the desktop does not pay for it; every colour is a token.
A view of notificationStore, the notification centre (sticky errors, 6 s auto-dismiss, click-to-open, do-not-disturb); Base UI's Toast would duplicate the store. notify() stays the one way in.
A launcher with a search field, a pinned grid and an A-Z list (decisions-themes.md, 2026-11-06), not a Base UI Menu.
A key-driven overlay: the dialog is the kit's PaletteDialog on Base UI; the list inside is hand-built until the palette moves onto Autocomplete, a later choice.
A key-driven overlay held open by the Alt key; no Base UI part matches.
A seek bar with a hover preview and a buffered range; Base UI's Slider has no equivalent.
A native app's own surface, drawn by the app behind it: black is its background, not a design colour.
A Linux window's own surface, painted by the app behind it: black is its background, not a design colour.
The page frame: a web page that sets no background of its own renders on white, whatever the theme.
The drawing canvas is white paper in every theme (and the text box over it), as the saved image is.

The remaining inline styles (79 after brief 87 moved four static ones to classes) are window frames and desktop-layer geometry, swatch and preview colours from data, and runtime custom properties (scratch audit, brief 87); the few static ones are listed in the outcome note.
